fit_paragraphs.text: Prof. Tsvetkov's TsvetShop lab works directly on the problems I have been building toward [advisor:Yulia Tsvetkov]. Her NAACL 2024 paper on context-aware decoding to reduce hallucination [paper:W4401042371] connects to my interest in faithfulness evaluation beyond translated English benchmarks [lib:interests], and her ACL 2024 work on identifying LLM knowledge gaps through multi-LLM collaboration [paper:W4402671287] points toward the kind of rigorous, language-aware evaluation I want to pursue [lib:interests]. My tokenizer-adaptation internship at Microsoft Research India [lib:cv] maps onto the multilingual tokenization fairness questions the lab addresses [advisor:Yulia Tsvetkov]. I would want to extend that work—adding vocabulary for Tamil and Kannada—within a research program that explicitly targets underserved languages [lib:interests].

Prof. Hajishirzi's H2Lab offers infrastructure I cannot access elsewhere [advisor:Hannaneh Hajishirzi]. The Dolma pretraining corpus [paper:W4402671286] and the OLMo open model [paper:W4402671236] would let me study data selection for Indian-language pretraining at scale—directly extending my finding that 6k added Kannada tokens improved QA F1 by 3.4 points at the same fine-tuning budget [lib:cv]. The OpenScholar retrieval-augmented system [paper:W7127589252] is a concrete proof-of-concept for the RAG-for-health-and-government direction I listed as a secondary interest [lib:interests]. The lab's explicit pillar of "Science of AI and evaluation" [advisor:Hannaneh Hajishirzi] also aligns with my evaluation work on Tamil–English code-switching [lib:cv].

sop.text:
In 2025 I built a Tamil–English code-switched evaluation set of 2,400 sentences and tested two open 7B models on it [lib:cv]. Both lost 18–26 points relative to monolingual Tamil baselines [lib:cv]. People in Chennai do not speak monolingual Tamil to a chatbot; they switch registers mid-sentence. That single result shaped everything I have done since: current evaluation benchmarks, almost all derived from translated English data, hide systematic failures for multilingual users [lib:interests].

That finding became a first-author workshop paper at an ACL-family conference [lib:cv]. More importantly, it pushed me to ask what sits upstream of evaluation: representation. At Microsoft Research India in summer 2026, mentored by Dr. Anjali Mehra, I worked on tokenizer adaptation for Kannada [lib:cv]. Extending a SentencePiece vocabulary with 6,000 Kannada-specific tokens cut the average token count per sentence by 41% and improved downstream QA F1 by 3.4 points at the same fine-tuning budget [lib:cv]. The practical lesson: a cheap, targeted change to the tokenizer can matter as much as expensive fine-tuning, and it is invisible to benchmarks that measure only English-proximate text [lib:interests].

In parallel, a Spring 2026 course project trained a wav2vec2-style model on 40 hours of Tamil radio audio and reached 31% WER on a held-out set [lib:cv]. That experiment confirmed a constraint I care about: for many Indian languages, spoken data dwarfs written data, and any serious adaptation pipeline has to handle audio [lib:interests].

For a PhD I want to pursue three connected directions. First, parameter-efficient and data-efficient adaptation of LLMs to low-resource Indian languages—tokenizer extension, vocabulary-aware PEFT, and targeted data selection [lib:interests]. Second, evaluation methodology that measures code-switching robustness, cultural grounding, and faithfulness rather than translated benchmark scores [lib:interests]. Third, speech-text models that can bootstrap from limited transcribed audio [lib:interests]. A secondary thread is retrieval-augmented generation for government and health information in Indian languages, where faithful grounding is especially consequential [lib:interests].

At UW Allen School I am drawn to two research groups. Prof. Tsvetkov's TsvetShop lab explicitly pursues NLP across linguistic and cultural boundaries [advisor:Yulia Tsvetkov]. Her work on reducing hallucination through context-aware decoding [paper:W4401042371] and on identifying LLM knowledge gaps through multi-LLM collaboration [paper:W4402671287] intersects with the faithfulness and evaluation thread I want to develop; I would aim to bring code-switching and low-resource Indic data into that evaluation framework. Prof. Hajishirzi's H2Lab built the OLMo open model [paper:W4402671236] and the Dolma pretraining corpus [paper:W4402671286], infrastructure that would let me study data selection for Indian-language pretraining at a scale unavailable to me now. The OpenScholar retrieval-augmented system [paper:W7127589252] is also a strong proof-of-concept for the RAG direction I listed as a secondary interest [lib:interests].

I am currently in my final year of a B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering at NIT Tiruchirappalli, with a CGPA of 9.21/10 placing me in the top 5% of the department [lib:profile]. I hold an Institute Merit Scholarship awarded in each of the past three years [lib:cv]. As a teaching assistant for a 120-student machine learning course I wrote supplementary material on tokenization; as organiser of the NIT Trichy NLP reading group I have worked through the papers that now anchor my research plans [lib:cv]. My technical stack—PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, PEFT/LoRA, SentencePiece, FAISS—covers the tools I would use from day one [lib:cv].

The questions I want to answer are concrete: how much can targeted tokenizer surgery improve a model's utility for a Tamil speaker, how do we build evaluation sets that catch failures invisible to English-derived benchmarks, and what does an efficient speech-text pipeline look like when your training data is 40 hours of radio rather than 40,000 hours of podcast? I want to spend the next five years on those questions at a program where open infrastructure and multilingual evaluation are already active research bets.

emails.subject: Prospective PhD student — multilingual tokenization and code-switching evaluation
emails.body:
Dear Prof. Tsvetkov,

I am Priya Raman, a final-year B.Tech student in Computer Science at NIT Tiruchirappalli (CGPA 9.21/10), applying to UW Allen School for Fall 2027. I am writing to ask whether you are planning to take PhD students this cycle.

My work sits at the intersection of tokenizer adaptation and multilingual evaluation. At Microsoft Research India in summer 2026 I extended a SentencePiece vocabulary with 6,000 Kannada tokens, cutting token counts by 41% and improving QA F1 by 3.4 points at the same fine-tuning budget. Earlier, a Tamil–English code-switched evaluation set I built showed 18–26 point drops for open 7B models versus monolingual baselines, leading to a first-author workshop paper at an ACL-family conference.

I read your NAACL 2024 paper "Trusting Your Evidence: Hallucinate Less with Context-aware Decoding" with close attention; the decoding-level intervention for faithfulness connects directly to evaluation gaps I observed in code-switched settings, and I would want to extend that line of work to Indic languages.

I would be glad to share my CV if that would be helpful. Thank you for your time.

Priya Raman

emails.subject: Prospective PhD student — low-resource LLM adaptation and multilingual evaluation
emails.body:
Dear Prof. Hajishirzi,

I am Priya Raman, a final-year B.Tech student in Computer Science at NIT Tiruchirappalli (CGPA 9.21/10), applying to UW Allen School for Fall 2027. I am writing to ask whether the H2Lab is planning to take PhD students this cycle.

My research focuses on efficient LLM adaptation for Indian languages. At Microsoft Research India in summer 2026 I worked on Kannada tokenizer adaptation—adding 6,000 vocabulary items cut token counts by 41% and improved QA F1 by 3.4 points. My earlier work built a Tamil–English code-switched evaluation set that revealed 18–26 point failures in open 7B models, published as a first-author workshop paper.

The Dolma corpus paper at ACL 2024 is directly relevant to questions I want to pursue: specifically, how data selection criteria affect representation of low-resource languages during pretraining, and whether targeted curation can close the gap my tokenizer experiments exposed. Access to OLMo's open infrastructure would make that research tractable.

I would be happy to share my CV at your convenience. Thank you for considering my message.

Priya Raman
